description: Answers "where do users drop off, and is it crashes?" in one place. Four flows, six charts: the journey Sankey gives the full inbound path to every screen and where journeys abandon; the journey funnel counts survivors at each of the seven stages; crashes-by-last-screen groups terminations by the screen the user was on when the previous run died (reported next launch, so it also covers hangs and OOM kills that leave no log in the session that died); screen-visits-by-name is the denominator — crash count alone ranks popular screens, crash count / visits ranks actually-risky ones. To analyse: join Sankey drop-off screens to crashes-by-last-screen on screen name, then normalise by visits. High abandonment + high crash rate = crash-driven funnel leak; high abandonment + low crash rate = UX or pricing. Filter terminations-by-reason to fatalCrash for real crashes. Crashes appear here as a grouped field metric rather than a Sankey terminal by design, since this workflow is meant to hold for any session strategy. APP_IOS_BUILT_IN_CRASH can in fact advance a multi-step flow, but only under sessionStrategy .activityBased() with the relaunch landing inside inactivityThresholdMins — see bd-shop-19, which does exactly that.
